findings.title: Disable instructions incorrectly promise that the guard remains active
findings.trigger: An operator follows the documented disable command expecting subsequent checker spawns to be blocked.
findings.execution_path: The plugin owns both the agent.spawn module and the classic PreToolUse guard in hooks/hooks.json. Disabling the plugin removes both registrations in subsequent sessions; shared .claude/settings.json contains no independent guard.
findings.consequence: BM checker spawns can proceed with their ordinary model while the operator believes the documented fail-closed block is active.
findings.evidence: README lines 61–63 equate disabling the entire plugin with removing the module-gate environment key. These differ: removing the gate can leave the enabled plugin's classic guard active, whereas disabling its owner removes that guard too. Tests invoke guard.mjs directly and cannot detect this lifecycle discrepancy.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that disabling the plugin restores ordinary BM checking. For a blocking mode, keep the plugin enabled and unset the module gate, or register an independent guard if blocking must survive plugin disablement.
findings.hypothesis: On a fresh session after plugin disablement, neither plugin hook loads and BM uses its original checker model. This follows from registration ownership but was not exercised against a live Claude runtime.

limitations: Did not independently run pytest in the read-only sandbox; inspected harness evidence reporting exit 0 and 2,432 passing tests on the exact head.
Live Claude plugin lifecycle, external BM callers, and model-gateway behavior could not be verified using only this working copy.
The guard checks an environment flag, not successful module registration. Passing unit tests therefore do not prove fail-closed behavior after host-loading failures or runtime upgrades.
